newsitem.title: FRANCE: Credit Foncier made H1 profit - reports.
newsitem.headline: Credit Foncier made H1 profit - reports.

text.p: Credit Foncier de France, the property lender due to be taken over by a state bank and then wound down, made an unexpected net profit of some 400 million francs in the first half, French newspapers reported on Friday.
The profit, compared with expectations of a loss, was due mainly to non-recurring items such as profits from the sale of the bank's local authority lending portfolio, Le Figaro said.
Credit Foncier was unavailable for comment.
The bank was due to issue first-half results on Friday morning after a board meeting the night before.
Business daily La Tribune Desfosses said Credit Foncier made a first-half net consolidated profit of more than 400 million francs and a basic profit of less than 700 million francs.
On Thursday, Credit Foncier declined to comment on a report in L'Agefi financial daily that it would announce a first-half profit of 200-to-400 million francs.
Credit Foncier shares were suspended on August 28 following a public offer of 70 francs per share for the lender by the Caisse des Depots et Consignations (CDC) state bank.
CDC's offer is aimed at taking over the assets and gradually winding down the bank, which lost 10.8 billion francs in 1995.
